articles.title: “Supervision till 16 isn’t control, it’s care”: Shilpa Shetty on the one internet rule parents should not ignore while raising children
articles.summary: For parents, giving a child a phone is rarely just about giving them a device. It also means giving them access to videos, games, social media, strang.
articles.body: For parents, giving a child a phone is rarely just about giving them a device. It also means giving them access to videos, games, social media, strangers, misinformation and content they may not yet know how to process. Actor Shilpa Shetty spoke about this balance on the occasion of Safer Internet Day in February this year, asking parents to look beyond simply restricting screen time.In a video shared on Instagram, she said she was speaking “not as a public figure, but as a concerned mother” and urged parents to have more open conversations about what children do online. “The Internet is a powerful teacher, a playground for creativity,” Shilpa said. “So with the pros comes the cons, and we must be aware of them.”“It can also expose young minds to things that they're not ready for. And as parents, our role isn't to just simply ban technology. It's to balance the access and exposure to it.” That balance, however, can be difficult.Parents want to protect their children, but children increasingly use the internet for schoolwork, entertainment, friendships and discovering the world around them. Taking the phone away may stop one problem temporarily, but it does not teach a child what to do when something disturbing appears on the screen.Shilpa's advice starts with knowing what a child is consuming. “Know what your child is watching, scrolling, consuming,” she said. She also stressed the importance of talking instead of relying entirely on restrictions. “Curiosity grows in silence, not in conversation,” she said in the video.“Supervision till 16, I believe, isn’t control. It’s care”The most striking part of Shilpa's message was her view on parental supervision. “Please use parental controls. But more importantly, build trust,” she said. “Supervision till 16, I believe, isn’t control. It’s care.” The statement raises an important question for parents: what should supervision actually look like?There is a difference between knowing what platforms a child uses and secretly reading every private conversation. There is also a difference between setting age-appropriate restrictions and monitoring a child so closely that they stop feeling trusted. Good digital supervision should ideally change as the child grows.A 10-year-old may need parents to decide which apps are appropriate. A 13-year-old may need help understanding privacy, online friendships and inappropriate content. A 15-year-old may need more independence, but still needs to know that a parent is available when something goes wrong. The aim should be to gradually transfer responsibility to the child rather than suddenly handing over complete freedom.Don't wait for the first online crisis to have the conversationOne practical mistake parents can make is talking about internet safety only after something happens. A child sees an inappropriate video. Someone sends a disturbing message. A stranger asks for a photograph. A friend shares a private image. Only then does the parent sit down for a serious conversation. By that point, the child may already be frightened about telling them.Instead, parents can have small, ordinary conversations long before there is a problem. Ask what they watched today. Which creator do they like? What games are they playing? What do their friends discuss online?Teach children what to do when something goes wrongInternet safety is not just about preventing children from seeing harmful content. It is also about preparing them for the moment they inevitably encounter something they were not expecting. Parents can teach a simple three-step response: Stop. Don't respond. Tell an adult. If someone online makes a child uncomfortable, asks for personal information, sends inappropriate material or pressures them to keep a conversation secret, the child should know they can leave the conversation and tell a trusted adult. Most importantly, parents should make one thing clear that telling the truth will not automatically result in the phone being taken away.Parental controls are useful, but they cannot replace parentingShilpa also urged parents to use parental controls. These tools can help parents manage age restrictions, purchases, screen time and access to certain content. But a parental-control setting cannot teach a child why a stranger asking for their school name is a red flag. It cannot explain why a viral video may be edited or false. And it cannot help a teenager deal with cyberbullying.That is why technology controls work best when paired with conversations. Parents can even involve older children in setting the rules. Instead of simply announcing, “You get one hour of screen time,” discuss when the phone can be used, which apps are allowed and what happens if a rule is broken. When children understand the reason behind a rule, they are more likely to follow it.One rule parents should avoidTrust does not mean giving children unlimited privacy at every age. But constant surveillance can also backfire. If a teenager knows that every message, search and photograph may be checked without warning, they may become better at hiding things rather than better at making safe choices. A healthier approach is to establish expectations in advance. Parents can tell children: “Your privacy matters, but your safety matters more. If I become worried about something serious, I may need to step in. I will tell you rather than secretly monitoring you.”That keeps the door open for intervention while respecting the child's growing independence.Teach children one important internet ruleShilpa said, “Teach them that not everything online is real, kind, or even safe.” That lesson covers much more than fake news. Children need to understand that people may present an edited version of their lives online. Influencers may be paid to promote products. Videos can be manipulated. Strangers may pretend to be someone else. A large number of followers does not make a person trustworthy. For teenagers especially, this can become a regular family conversation rather than a one-time lecture.Shilpa ended her message by saying she does not have all the answers but wants to “start a real conversation”. She also urged parents to stop “parenting in isolation” and work towards raising “digitally aware and not digitally addicted children”. The goal cannot realistically be to keep children away from the internet. They will eventually use it for education, work, friendships and everyday life. The more useful goal is to raise a child who knows when to put the phone down, when to question what they see, when to block someone, when to ask for help and when an online interaction has crossed a line.Looking for trusted parenting advice? articles.title: Quote of the day by Barack Obama: "Making your mark on the world is hard. If it were easy, everybody would…" - a powerful message about failure and success
articles.summary: US News: Barack Obama's words are a genuinely honest reminder that meaningful achievement rarely happens quickly, and almost never without a real setback along.
articles.body: Barack Obama's words are a genuinely honest reminder that meaningful achievement rarely happens quickly, and almost never without a real setback along the way. "Making your mark on the world is hard," he said. "If it were easy, everybody would do it. But it's not. It takes patience, it takes commitment and it comes with plenty of failure along the way." This line comes from a college commencement address he delivered in 2012, reported by NPR that same year in a segment covering that season's graduation speeches. Obama continued the thought considerably further, saying, "The real test is not whether you avoid this failure, because you won't. It's whether you let it harden or shame you into inaction, or whether you learn from it, whether you choose to persevere." Making a lasting contribution to anything worthwhile, whether through a career or a genuinely creative pursuit, usually demands considerably more than raw talent alone.Quote of the day by Barack Obama"Making your mark on the world is hard. If it were easy, everybody would do it. But it's not. It takes patience, it takes commitment and it comes with plenty of failure along the way"What is the meaning of Barack Obama's quoteObama is genuinely saying that making a meaningful impact is difficult precisely because it requires qualities not everyone is actually willing to develop. If success were genuinely easy, almost everyone would achieve exactly the same level of recognition, and the fact that it is difficult means people genuinely have to stay committed even when results are not immediate. His reference to failure is particularly important here. A setback is presented not as evidence that someone should automatically quit, but as a genuinely expected part of pursuing anything actually worthwhile.Why patience genuinely matters when pursuing successMany genuine goals take considerably longer than people initially expect. Whether someone is building a career or learning an entirely new skill, real progress can be genuinely uneven, and there may be long stretches where the effort produces very little visible result. Patience is what allows people to genuinely keep working through those stretches, rather than abandoning a real goal simply because success has not arrived quickly enough.Why commitment matters more than temporary motivationMotivation genuinely changes from one day to the next. There will be days when working toward a goal feels genuinely exciting, and others when it feels considerably more exhausting or frustrating. Commitment provides something genuinely more stable than either mood. It means continuing to actually take action even when enthusiasm is temporarily missing, and that consistency can be exactly what separates a short-lived attempt from a genuinely long-term pursuit.Why failure is genuinely part of the journeyObama's quote never presents failure as an unusual event. Instead, he describes it as something that genuinely comes "along the way," and that distinction genuinely matters. A failed attempt does not necessarily mean the overall goal has actually failed. It can reveal what genuinely needs to change, or which approach was unlikely to work in the first place. Failure becomes genuinely useful specifically when people are willing to actually examine it, rather than simply fearing it outright, which is really the whole point of his fuller continuation about not letting failure "harden or shame you into inaction."Why making a real difference genuinely takes timeSome of the most genuinely meaningful accomplishments are built gradually. A person may spend real years developing expertise before receiving any recognition at all, and a creative project may genuinely require countless attempts before it actually reaches its potential. The final result can genuinely make the whole process look effortless from the outside, when behind it usually sit real years of work that stayed largely invisible to everyone else watching.The genuine difference between success and instant resultsModern culture can genuinely make success appear immediate. People often see only the finished product rather than the actual years of preparation sitting behind it. Obama's quote genuinely challenges that perception by putting the real emphasis back on the process itself. Patience and commitment matter because meaningful progress is very often genuinely cumulative, and small improvement repeated over a genuinely long period can eventually produce a result that would have been completely impossible through occasional bursts of effort alone.How to genuinely handle a setback without simply giving upA real setback can be genuinely discouraging, particularly once someone has invested considerable time into something. One genuinely useful approach is to separate the actual goal from the method used to reach it. If one approach genuinely fails, it does not automatically mean the goal itself was impossible. Sometimes the real strategy simply needs to change, and this mindset genuinely lets failure become useful information rather than some kind of final verdict on your ability.What this quote genuinely teaches about perseveranceGenuine perseverance was never simply about continuing to do exactly the same thing regardless of the actual results. Effective perseverance genuinely involves learning and adapting along the way. A person can genuinely remain committed to a goal while still changing their actual methods, seeking real advice, or trying a considerably different approach entirely. That combination of persistence and real flexibility is what genuinely makes a long-term goal considerably more achievable.Other popular quotes by Barack Obama"Change will not come if we wait for some other person, or if we wait for some other time. We are the ones we've been waiting for. We are the change that we seek.""Focusing your life solely on making a buck shows a poverty of ambition. It asks too little of yourself.""You can't let your failures define you. You have to let your failures teach you.""If you're walking down the right path and you're willing to keep walking, eventually you'll make progress."How to apply Barack Obama's lessonBe genuinely patient, giving a meaningful goal enough real time to actually develop properly. Stay genuinely committed, continuing to work even while motivation naturally fluctuates from one day to the next. Expect real setbacks, since genuine difficulty never automatically means actual failure. Learn honestly from a genuine mistake, treating an unsuccessful attempt as useful information rather than a final verdict, and adapt your actual approach once the evidence genuinely suggests something is not working. Focus on real progress rather than instant results, since small improvement genuinely accumulates over time, and avoid comparing your own timeline with someone else's, since their genuinely visible achievement may well hide years of invisible work behind it.Why Barack Obama's quote remains relevantThe genuine pressure to achieve quickly can make an entirely ordinary setback feel like a major failure. Obama's words offer a considerably more realistic perspective instead, that genuinely important achievement is difficult, takes real time, and rarely happens without some actual failure along the way. That does not mean every genuinely difficult goal should be pursued indefinitely regardless of the evidence. It means real difficulty and setback should never automatically be interpreted as reasons to simply quit. Sometimes the actual process of trying, failing, learning and trying again is genuinely exactly how meaningful progress happens. Making your mark was never really about avoiding failure altogether. It requires having enough real patience and genuine commitment to actually learn from failure and keep moving forward regardless.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Akhilesh's 'chavanni' jab: Can Jayant Chaudhary be BJP’s trump card in western UP?
articles.summary: India News: Akhilesh Yadav may have intended \"chavanni\" as a put-down, but in Uttar Pradesh politics, old coins have a habit of changing hands and sometimes gaini.
articles.body: Akhilesh Yadav may have intended "chavanni" as a put-down, but in Uttar Pradesh politics, old coins have a habit of changing hands and sometimes gaining value in the process. Three years after Jayant Chaudhary insisted he was no "chavanni" to be flipped, the coin metaphor has made a comeback, this time from his former ally, just as the RLD chief prepares for another electoral test in western UP.The row began when Akhilesh, without naming Jayant, said: "Humne chavanni ka rupya bana diya tha, tab bhi humein chhod kar chale gaye wo" — we turned a 25-paise coin into a rupee, yet they left us. The remark was widely seen as a jibe at the RLD chief, who had once used the same "chavanni" metaphor while rejecting speculation that he could switch sides.Jayant's response was swift. "Siyasat ki ladai mein kuch saste shabd bolne hi the, to mera naam lekar bol dete, koi baat nahi thi," he said. He accused Akhilesh of targeting the Jat community and added: "Main is ahankar ko dekh chuka hoon kareeb se aur maanta hoon aisa aacharan sirf patan laata hai" — I have seen this arrogance from close quarters and believe such conduct only leads to downfall.Meanwhile, Uttar Pradesh CM Yogi Adityanath also jumped in and hit back at Akhilesh, saying the language used against political opponents was making a "mockery of democracy" while describing the remark as an insult to Jayant, the legacy of Chaudhary Charan Singh and the farming community.The exchange may look like little more than pre-election sparring. But it points to a bigger question: why is Jayant Chaudhary important enough for both sides to keep talking about him?Jayant is no longer merely a smaller ally being wooed by rival camps. He is a Union minister, heads a party that won both Lok Sabha seats it contested in 2024 and carries the Chaudhary family name into a region where Jats and farmers remain central to the political arithmetic.So, ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly election, the real question is less about whether Akhilesh turned a "chavanni" into a rupee and more about how much political currency that rupee can buy in western UP.The 'coin' that changed handsIn the 2024 Lok Sabha election, Jayant's RLD posted a 100% strike rate, winning both seats it contested while in alliance with the BJP.But the picture was very different in the assembly elections.In 2017, the party was reduced to a marginal force in Uttar Pradesh, winning just one seat with around 1.5% of the vote share.However, in 2022, as it entered an alliance with the Samajwadi Party, the RLD contested 33 seats and won eight, with its vote share rising to nearly 3%.But the revival was not entirely an SP creation.Jayant had already begun rebuilding his political base, and the 2020-21 farmers' protests gave him an opportunity to re-establish himself as one of western UP's prominent political faces. Through kisan panchayats and sustained attacks on the NDA government over the farm laws and sugarcane dues, he reconnected with sections of a Jat electorate that had moved towards the BJP after the communal polarisation following the 2013 Muzaffarnagar riots.The SP-RLD alliance therefore worked both ways. The SP provided the RLD electoral space and organisational support, while Jayant offered the SP access to a Jat political network in a region where the BJP had built a formidable base.The numbers underline both the limits and value of that alliance. The RLD won eight of the 33 seats it contested in 2022, but the BJP won all 25 seats that the RLD lost.The RLD had regained relevance in pockets of western UP, but it was nowhere close to being a statewide challenger.Akhilesh may therefore have a point when he says the SP helped turn the RLD's "chavanni" into a rupee. But that is only half the transaction.Jayant brought the SP something that could not be created simply through seat-sharing - a political bridge to sections of the Jat electorate and the symbolic capital of the Chaudhary family.How BJP 'won' RLD chief's heartIn February 2024, the BJP and RLD announced their alliance, with the BJP offering the smaller party two Lok Sabha seats and a Rajya Sabha berth.The announcement came shortly after the Centre conferred the Bharat Ratna on former prime minister Chaudhary Charan Singh, a move Jayant publicly welcomed.He immediately posted on X: "Dil jeet liya" - won the heart.When asked whether the post meant the RLD would join the BJP, Jayant replied: "Koi kasar rehti hai? Aaj main kis muh se inkaar karoon aapke sawalon ko?" - Is there anything left? How can I deny your questions today?The RLD then contested Baghpat and Bijnor in the 2024 Lok Sabha election and won both.For the BJP, however, the bigger prize was a political intermediary who could speak to sections of the Jat electorate on behalf of the NDA while carrying the Chaudhary name.The BJP's relationship with Jayant Chaudhary's party and family had also undergone a dramatic reversal.In 2014, the BJP swept western Uttar Pradesh, defeating then-RLD chief Ajit Singh in Baghpat and his son Jayant in Mathura. Five years later, the father-son duo suffered another setback, losing in Muzaffarnagar and Baghpat respectively.But the saffron party subsequently lost some ground among Jats amid the farmers' protests and the long-running demand for reservation.Jayant's entry into the NDA therefore gave the BJP a recognised Jat face at a time when the opposition was trying to rebuild a broader farmer-minority coalition in the region.Why Jats matter in western UPThere is no recent official caste census providing a definitive figure for the Jat population in Uttar Pradesh. Estimates commonly put Jats at around 2% of the state's population, but their concentration in western UP gives them much greater political weight in the region. Estimates have put their share at roughly 17-18% in the area often described as "Jatland".They heavily sway the electoral outcomes of roughly 40 to 45 assembly seats and about 10 to 12 Lok Sabha (parliamentary) seats in western UP.There is also a historical reason the Jat vote matters.Before the 2013 Muzaffarnagar riots, the politics of Chaudhary Charan Singh and later Ajit Singh rested in part on a cross-community farmer coalition involving Jats and Muslims. The riots fractured that relationship and pushed many Jats towards the BJP.The farmers' movement briefly reopened the possibility of a Jat-Muslim political convergence that the SP-RLD alliance tried to convert into votes in 2022.Jayant's subsequent move to the NDA, however, made that opposition combination considerably harder to sustain.For the BJP, therefore, Jayant may be useful not simply because he can attract Jats, but because his presence can also complicate the social coalition Akhilesh is trying to build.The Jayant question in Akhilesh's PDA strategyThat brings the RLD directly into Akhilesh's larger PDA strategy — Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak — which seeks to bring backward classes, Dalits and minorities together while reducing the SP's dependence on its traditional Yadav base.The 2024 Lok Sabha election demonstrated the potential of that strategy, with the SP emerging as the largest party in Uttar Pradesh.For the BJP, the challenge ahead of 2027 will be to prevent that coalition from consolidating, particularly in regions where the party faces a more competitive opposition.Jayant is one piece of that counter-strategy.The RLD, meanwhile, appears keen to expand beyond its traditional Jat base. Its outreach has included Gurjars and other communities, while party leaders have spoken of a broader AJGR formula - Ahir, Jat, Gurjar and Rajput - along with efforts to reach Dalits and Muslims.Why September 3 rally mattersThat is why the RLD's September 3 'Swabhiman Rally' in Saharanpur mattered beyond its immediate spat with Akhilesh.The rally was an attempt to demonstrate that Jayant can still mobilise on his own political terms rather than functioning merely as a BJP ally.And Jayant used the "chavanni" controversy to turn criticism into an argument for relevance."Jo abhi gaaliyan de rahe hain, abhi to sun lo... sahi samay par nipat lenge," he said — those abusing us should listen for now; they will be dealt with at the appropriate time. He then added that the fact that opposition leaders kept mentioning the RLD showed that the party was working in the "right place and in the right direction."(function(){function e(){window.addEventListener(`message`,function(e){if(e.data[`datawrapper-height`]!==void 0){var t=document.querySelectorAll(`iframe`);for(var n in e.data[`datawrapper-height`])for(var r=0,i;i=t[r];r++)if(i.contentWindow===e.source){var a=e.data[`datawrapper-height`][n]+`px`;i.style.height=a}}})}e()})();But the more significant part of his pitch was directed at farmers, the community most closely associated with the Chaudhary family's political legacy.Calling on farmers to identify their "true supporters" and choose a strong political advocate, Jayant said: "Farmers are in a majority and governments are made and unmade on their strength, but the hard reality is that the farmers’ lobby is weak in political corridors. Therefore, farmers need to choose a strong advocate for their cause."This could be seen as more than a regular rallying cry. It was a reminder of what Jayant believes his political value rests on: being the voice of a region and a community larger than the RLD's current electoral footprint.But how much is Jayant worth?The 2027 seat-sharing exercise could be the clearest measure yet of Jayant's political "worth".A meaningful allocation of seats would suggest that the BJP believes the RLD's organisation can add value across western UP. A sharply limited share, on the other hand, would indicate that the BJP sees little reason to give Jayant enough room to build an independent base.Jayant also has something to prove.The RLD's two Lok Sabha victories in 2024 demonstrated that the party could convert its alliance with the BJP into electoral success. The next test is whether it can build enough support beyond those two constituencies to negotiate from a position of strength.Now, ahead of the 2027 elections, the question is whether Jayant can convert that symbolic capital into enough independent political influence to remain indispensable to the BJP.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: An Australian woman bought cleared sugarcane land and planted trees; 10 years later, 119,000 trees transformed it into a rainforest home to flying-foxes
articles.summary: Rest of World News: Annie Schoenberger bought cleared land near Wonga Beach in Queensland, Australia, with a simple but ambitious goal of bringing rainforest back to a pr.
articles.body: Annie Schoenberger bought cleared land near Wonga Beach in Queensland, Australia, with a simple but ambitious goal of bringing rainforest back to a property once used for sugarcane. What followed was a decade-long restoration effort at her NightWings Rainforest Centre, where native trees were planted with the help of Rainforest Rescue, volunteers and supporters. More than 119,000 trees have now been planted across 18 hectares, gradually replacing the cleared agricultural landscape with young rainforest habitat. The project has also attracted native wildlife and helped restore wetland areas and improve water quality. In May 2026, the restoration reached another major milestone when the Queensland Government recognised the 18-hectare area as being of high nature conservation value, giving the recovering vegetation Category A protection under Queensland's vegetation management framework.From cleared sugarcane land to a young rainforestSchoenberger purchased the property in 2014 after much of the land had been cleared for sugarcane farming. She wanted to restore the landscape to lowland Daintree rainforest and create habitat for native wildlife. Restoration work began in 2015, followed by the first community tree-planting event in 2016. Rainforest Rescue became a major partner in the effort, helping organise planting events, supply rainforest seedlings and bring volunteers together to restore the former agricultural land.The original restoration target was around 15 hectares, but the area eventually expanded to 18 hectares. Instead of establishing a conventional plantation, the project focused on planting a diverse selection of native rainforest species that could gradually recreate the structure and ecological functions of the original forest.More than 119,000 trees planted over a decadeThe transformation was built through repeated planting efforts rather than a single large-scale operation. Over 10 years, volunteers, conservation workers and supporters returned to NightWings to put thousands of native seedlings into the ground.Rainforest Rescue's latest 2026 update says more than 119,000 trees had been planted at NightWings, with the final planting completed in 2025. The organisation says the decade-long effort involved hundreds of people who helped Schoenberger turn the cleared property into a growing rainforest landscape.The planting has also focused on species diversity. At a 2023 community planting day, more than 140 people planted 3,300 trees representing about 90 rainforest species. Such diversity is important because rainforest restoration is intended to recreate a functioning ecosystem rather than simply increase the number of trees.Wildlife began using the recovering habitatAs vegetation grew, the restored property began providing habitat and food resources for wildlife. NightWings is particularly connected to the spectacled flying-fox, a species Schoenberger has cared for through her wildlife rehabilitation work.Southern cassowaries have also been recorded at the property. A juvenile cassowary was photographed at NightWings in 2018, with Rainforest Rescue describing the sighting as particularly significant because it was the first recorded sighting south of the Daintree River in more than four decades. Later observations have continued to demonstrate that native wildlife is using the recovering landscape.Other fauna recorded around the property include various birds, mammals, reptiles, frogs and bats. Surveys have recorded more than 75 fauna species, including several species listed as endangered, vulnerable or near threatened.The wildlife records do not mean that every species returned solely because of the restoration, but they provide evidence that the recovering vegetation is being used as habitat.The restoration helped rebuild wetland habitatTree planting was only one part of the restoration. Wetland habitat at NightWings has also been restored, adding another type of ecosystem to the property.Rainforest Rescue has reported improvements in water quality associated with the restoration, including reduced sediment and turbidity entering nearby waterways. Re-establishing vegetation can help stabilise soil, slow runoff and create conditions that support healthier waterways.The location is also important because the property sits within the Wet Tropics region of Queensland, an area known for its exceptional rainforest biodiversity and its ecological connection to surrounding coastal environments.A former farm became a wildlife corridorThe restoration was intended to do more than improve a single property. Re-establishing rainforest on cleared land can help reconnect fragmented habitat, giving wildlife additional areas through which to move, feed and shelter.NightWings forms part of the broader effort to restore lowland rainforest in the Daintree region, where agricultural and other development have historically removed or fragmented sections of native vegetation.For Schoenberger, the project also had a personal connection. Her work caring for flying-foxes helped shape her desire to create a landscape where native fruiting trees could provide food and habitat for wildlife rather than leaving the animals dependent entirely on fragmented natural areas.The 18 hectares gained conservation protectionThe biggest development came in May 2026, when the Queensland Government formally recognised the restored NightWings vegetation as an area of high nature conservation value under the Vegetation Management Act 1999.The 18 hectares are now mapped as Category A vegetation on Queensland's regulated vegetation management map. This gives the restored vegetation a higher level of protection against clearing and formally recognises the conservation importance of the recovering forest.The designation is particularly notable because the land was once used for agriculture. A landscape that had been cleared for sugarcane is now recognised by the state for its conservation value after a decade of restoration.A decade turned a cleared landscape into a restoration successNightWings shows how long-term restoration can gradually change land that had been cleared for agriculture. Schoenberger bought the former sugarcane property, began restoring it with conservation partners and continued the effort for a decade as volunteers planted tens of thousands of native trees.By the completion of planting in 2025, Rainforest Rescue reported more than 119,000 trees planted across the restoration area. In 2026, the 18 hectares of restored vegetation gained recognition as an area of high nature conservation value and Category A protection.The forest is still young and its ecological development will continue for decades, but the transformation is already substantial. What began as cleared sugarcane land is now a growing rainforest landscape providing habitat for native wildlife and carrying formal recognition for its conservation value.Catch the latest World News and Live updates.
